findings.title: argon2i_32 accepts nb_blocks below the required minimum, causing heap buffer overflow in crypto_argon2
findings.evidence: argon2i_32 passes the caller-supplied nb_blocks unvalidated into crypto_argon2_config.nb_blocks (c_monocypher.pyx:328) and sizes the work area as malloc(nb_blocks * 1024) (c_monocypher.pyx:345). Every other length field is bounds-checked with _validate_u32 (lines 334-342), but nb_blocks is not, even though monocypher.h:160 requires nb_blocks >= 8 * nb_lanes and the binding hard-codes nb_lanes = 1 (line 330). In monocypher.c:752-754 a small nb_blocks makes segment_size = nb_blocks/4/1 and lane_size = segment_size*4 both zero for nb_blocks in [0,3], yet the unconditional first-fill loop at monocypher.c:776-782 still writes blocks[0].a and blocks[1].a, i.e. 2 * 1024 bytes, regardless of lane_size. Therefore argon2i_32(1, ...) allocates only 1024 bytes but 2048 bytes are written -> 1024-byte heap overflow; nb_blocks=0 calls malloc(0) and still writes 2048 bytes -> heap overflow (or immediate NULL dereference if malloc(0) returns NULL). The same lane_size == 0 also makes last_block = blocks + lane_size - 1 = blocks - 1 (monocypher.c:902), so store64_le_buf reads 1024 bytes before the allocation (out-of-bounds read) and feeds that heap memory into the returned key via extended_hash for nb_blocks 0-3. Any application that lets an untrusted party influence the Argon2 cost parameters (e.g. a password-hashing service exposing tuning options) reaches this with a single call such as argon2i_32(1, 1, b'pw', b'saltsalt'), corrupting the CPython heap and enabling memory-disclosure/code-execution attacks.
